newsitem.title: FRANCE: Asset sales, op activities drive Paribas pft return.
newsitem.headline: Asset sales, op activities drive Paribas pft return.

text.p: French holding company Groupe Paribas returned convincingly to profit last year, reversing a big 1995 loss incurred from writedowns on loss-making investments.
An accelerated programme of asset sales -- aided by a strong French stock market-- along with rises in operating activities at all its business units, lifted the company out of the red.
Paribas said it earned 4.35 billion francs ($763.9 million) in 1996 after a four billion franc loss the year before. In 1994, the company earned 1.75 billion francs.

Paribas indicated that asset sales would continue to contribute to its earnings in the years ahead, saying that unrealised capital gains from its equity portfolio increased last year, despite its many asset sales.
It said its goals for asset disposals adopted for the next three years were already reached.
Paribas' profits last year could have been higher were it not for 2.5 billion francs of exceptional provisions taken by its Cie Bancaire unit "to eliminate real estate risks".
The company also took provisions to cover the cost of transition to a single European currency.

Paribas' 1995 loss, a rare event at the company, was due mostly to a hefty 2.13 billion franc provision to write down the value of its 31 percent stake in diversified conglomerate Cie de Navigation Mixte.

Other 1995 charges included 1.9 billion francs against losses at its Cogedim property development unit and 1.19 billion francs for assets transferred from its Credit du Nord unit, which it has since agreed to sell to French commercial bank Societe Generale.
But since the writedown of its investments, Paribas has taken majority control of Mixte and recorded significant capital gains from selling many of its assets.
Paribas' sale of assets held by Mixte allowed it to recoup cash equal to the 8.7 billion takeover of Mixte, which was originally financed with debt.
It has also moved to isolate itself from property losses at its various units.
The company said in a statement that in 1996 it rebuilt the financial resources of its flagship banking unit Banque Paribas. ($ = 5.694 French Francs)
